body.name: Exact response-type and linear-program certificate
body.construction: Enumerate the \(36\) reduced columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b)\in\{a,b,\star\}^2\times\{0,1\}^2\), the \(144\) saturated columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b,r_{c,1},r_{c,2})\in\{a,b,c\}^2\times\{0,1\}^4\), and the \(72\) common-response columns \( (x_1,x_2,y_a,y_b,r_c)\in\{a,b,c\}^2\times\{0,1\}^3\). For each list form its zero-one observed-cell incidence matrix \(G\), impose \(G\omega=p^{\mathrm w}\), \(\omega\ge0\), and \(\mathbf 1^\top\omega=1\), and minimize and maximize \(\sum_f\omega_f(y_b(f)-y_a(f))\). In the saturated program the lower endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((a,a,0,0,0,0)\) and \((c,c,1,0,1,0)\), while the upper endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((a,a,0,1,0,0)\) and \((c,c,0,1,1,0)\). The valid inequalities \(\tau\le1\) and \(\tau\ge-E[Y_a]\ge-1/2\), where \(P(Y_a=0)\ge P(X_1=a\text{ or }X_2=a)\ge1/2\), certify those saturated optima. Under the common-response restriction the lower endpoint is attained by mass \(1/2\) on each of \((c,a,0,0,1)\) and \((a,c,0,0,0)\), and the upper endpoint by the same two exposure-response columns with \(y_b=1\). The observed constraints make \(\{X_1=c,r_c=1\}\) and \(\{X_2=c,r_c=0\}\) disjoint events of total probability one and force \(Y_a=0\), certifying \(0\le\tau\le1\).
